doc.tool: Current state with the task camera (global layout) and wrist (close range) {{image_size}}x{{image_size}} images. Pixels (row, col) in these images feed back_project.

doc.code:
Per arm: <arm>_eef_pos (m, world), <arm>_eef_quat (xyzw), <arm>_joint_pos, <arm>_gripper_width, <arm>_gripper_command; success, env_steps, table_z, home_eef_pos.

Example:
    st = get_state()
    print(st["robot0_eef_pos"], st["robot0_gripper_width"], st["success"])

agentview and wrist, each {rgb uint8[512,512,3], depth float32[512,512] m, intrinsic_K 3x3, extrinsic_cam2world 4x4}, plus get_state's fields.

Example:
    obs = get_observation()
    rgb, depth = obs["agentview"]["rgb"], obs["agentview"]["depth"]
    K = obs["agentview"]["intrinsic_K"]; T = obs["agentview"]["extrinsic_cam2world"]

prompt.description: What to segment, e.g. 'red cube' (or give point)

point.description: A positive point [row, col] instead of a prompt

doc.tool: SAM3 segmentation of the current 512x512 camera image. Give exactly one of a text prompt or a positive point [row, col]. The top mask is projected through the depth world map; world_xyz is the median over mask pixels. Returns an overlay image.
doc.code:
SAM3 mask of a text prompt (or a point [row, col]) in the current image: found, score, box, mask, centroid_rowcol, world_xyz (median through the depth).

Example:
    m = segment("red cube")
    if m["found"]:
        print(m["world_xyz"], m["score"])

z_min.description: Region mode: keep pixels with world z >= z_min

z_max.description: Region mode: keep pixels with world z <= z_max

doc.tool: World xyz of a pixel (row, col; row 0 = top) in the current 512x512 camera image, from the depth world map. Region mode: row_range + col_range (+ optional z_min/z_max) returns the midpoint of world xy over that window and the median z.
doc.code:
World xyz of pixel (row, col) of the current 512x512 image through its depth.

Example:
    print(back_project(256, 300)["world_xyz"]) Region mode: row_range + col_range (+ z_min / z_max) returns center_xyz (midpoint of world x and y, median z).

arm.description: 'robot0' or 'robot1' on the two-arm tasks (required there); omit on one arm

doc.tool: Whether move_to could reach a world xyz from the arm's current joints (IK only; nothing moves). status unreachable means move_to would refuse it; unknown means the check could not run.
doc.code:
Whether the TCP can reach a world position (IK by the ik service; unknown without --ik).

Example:
    r = preview_reach([0.05, 0.02, 0.95])
    if r["status"] == "unreachable":
        print(r["message"])

arm.description: 'robot0' or 'robot1' on the two-arm tasks (required there); omit on one arm

quat_xyzw.description: Absolute world orientation to reach (default: keep)

rotvec.description: Instead: a world-frame turn, axis x angle, rad, from the current orientation

gripper.description: Set the held gripper command first (default: keep)

doc.tool: Closed-loop servo of the TCP to a world xyz, holding the orientation (or turning by rotvec, a world-frame axis-angle in rad). The server refuses a target more than {{max_move}} m away, outside the table workspace or below the z floor; split long moves. gripper sets the held command first.
doc.code:
Closed-loop OSC_POSE servo of the TCP to a world position, holding the orientation unless one is given; refused beyond the per-call cap, outside the workspace or below the table.

Example:
    move_to([0.05, 0.02, 0.95], gripper="open")
    r = move_to([0.05, 0.02, 0.83])
    print(r["final_dist_m"])

arm.description: 'robot0' or 'robot1' on the two-arm tasks (required there); omit on one arm

quat_xyzw.description: Absolute world orientation to reach (default: keep)

rotvec.description: Instead: a world-frame turn, axis x angle, rad, from the current orientation

gripper.description: Set the held gripper command first (default: keep)

doc.tool: Translate the TCP by a world-frame [dx, dy, dz] in metres (+z up; in the task camera +x runs toward the image bottom and +y toward the image right: on the one-arm tasks +x is away from robot0 and +y to its left, on the two-arm tasks +y runs from robot0 toward robot1; at most {{max_move}} m per call), holding the orientation. gripper sets the held command first.
doc.code:
Servo the TCP by a world-frame offset, holding the orientation; the same limits as move_to.

Example:
    move_delta([0, 0, 0.1])                    # lift 10 cm
    move_delta([0, 0, 0], rotvec=[0, 0, 0.5])  # turn the wrist 0.5 rad

close.description: true closes and holds, false opens

arm.description: 'robot0' or 'robot1' on the two-arm tasks (required there); omit on one arm

steps.description: Control steps to drive the fingers (default 15)

doc.tool: Hold the arm and open or close its gripper (up to `steps` control steps; the fingers stop on a grasped object). The command stays in force for later moves: carry with close.
doc.code:
Open or close one gripper and hold; the command stays in force for later moves.

Example:
    r = set_gripper(True)
    print(r["gripper_width"])  # near 0: closed on nothing

doc.tool: Camera calibration (intrinsic K and cam-to-world extrinsic for the 512x512 image; depth is metric) for the current step.
doc.code:
OpenCV intrinsics and camera-to-world extrinsic for the upright image.

Example:
    meta = get_camera_meta("agentview")
    K, T = meta["intrinsic_K"], meta["extrinsic_cam2world"]

robosuite's robot*_ observations (joint state, eef pose, gripper); no object poses.

Example:
    o = raw_obs()
    print(o["robot0_eef_pos"], o["robot0_gripper_qpos"])

Upright RGB (and metric depth) of a camera.

Example:
    rgb, depth = render_camera("wrist", 256, 256, depth=True)

One raw composite action: per arm 6 OSC_POSE deltas in [-1, 1] then the gripper (+1 close, -1 open).

Example:
    step([0, 0, 0.5, 0, 0, 0, -1])  # up 2.5 cm, gripper open (one arm)

object_name.description: The object in words, e.g. 'red cube'

return_bbox_extent.description: Also return the bounding-box extent (default false)

doc.tool: Pose of an object named in words, from SAM3 and depth: [position (3,), quaternion_wxyz (4,), bbox_extent (3,) or null]. The quaternion is identity: use the grasp quaternion, or [0, 0, 1, 0] (gripper down), when placing.
doc.code:
Get the pose of an object in the environment from a natural language description (SAM3 + depth).
The quaternion is identity: disregard it and use the grasp quaternion or [0, 0, 1, 0] (wxyz, gripper down) for placement.

Args:
    object_name: the object, e.g. "red cube".
    return_bbox_extent: also return the extent.

Returns:
    [position (3,), quaternion_wxyz (4,), bbox_extent (3,) or None]: world metres, full side lengths.

Example:
    pos, quat, ext = get_object_pose("green cube", return_bbox_extent=True)

object_name.description: The object in words, e.g. 'red cube'

return_bbox_extent.description: Also return the bounding-box extent (default false)

doc.tool: Privileged: the simulator's pose of an object named in words: [position (3,), quaternion_wxyz (4,), bbox_extent (3,) or null].
doc.code:
Get the pose of an object from the simulator (privileged).

Returns:
    [position (3,), quaternion_wxyz (4,), bbox_extent (3,) or None].

Example:
    pos, quat, ext = get_object_pose("red cube", return_bbox_extent=True)

arm.description: 'robot0' or 'robot1' on the two-arm tasks (required there); omit on one arm

doc.tool: A grasp of an object named in words: [position (3,), quaternion_wxyz (4,)] for goto_pose. With a grasp server the best planned grasp, else the object's centre with the gripper pointing down.
doc.code:
Sample a grasp pose for an object from a natural language description. Use its quaternion.

Returns:
    [position (3,), quaternion_wxyz (4,)].

Example:
    pos, quat = sample_grasp_pose("red cube")
    goto_pose(pos, quat, z_approach=0.1)

arm.description: 'robot0' or 'robot1' on the two-arm tasks (required there); omit on one arm

doc.tool: Privileged: a grasp of an object named in words, from the simulator: its position with the gripper pointing down.
doc.code:
Sample a grasp pose for an object (privileged: the simulator's position, gripper down [0, 0, 1, 0]).

Example:
    pos, quat = sample_grasp_pose("red cube")

position.description: World [x, y, z] of the grip point, m

z_approach.description: First stop this far back along the approach axis, m (default 0)

arm.description: 'robot0' or 'robot1' on the two-arm tasks (required there); omit on one arm

doc.tool: Go to a gripper pose (position and wxyz orientation); with z_approach first stop that far back along the approach axis. Long moves run as straight legs.
doc.code:
Go to pose. There is no need to call a second goto_pose with the same pose after calling it with z_approach.

Args:
    position: (3,) XYZ in meters.
    quaternion_wxyz: (4,) WXYZ unit quaternion.
    z_approach: first arrive z_approach metres back along the gripper's approach axis.

Example:
    goto_pose(pos, quat, z_approach=0.1)

arm.description: 'robot0' or 'robot1' on the two-arm tasks (required there); omit on one arm

doc.tool: Move the gripper back to its start position, pointing down.
doc.code:
Move the robot to a safe home pose.

Example:
    home_pose()

arm.description: 'robot0' or 'robot1' on the two-arm tasks (required there); omit on one arm

doc.code:
Open gripper fully.

Example:

arm.description: 'robot0' or 'robot1' on the two-arm tasks (required there); omit on one arm

Close gripper fully.

doc.code:
Solve inverse kinematics for the gripper (the ik service).

Returns:
    joints: 7 joint angles.

Example:

Move the arm to a joint configuration (the grip site servos to the pose those joints give; OSC_POSE arms).

Example:

arm.description: 'robot0' or 'robot1' on the two-arm tasks (required there); omit on one arm

doc.code:
Plan joint waypoints [N, 7] between two poses (a straight line in 2 cm steps, IK per waypoint).

Example:

    move_along_trajectory(traj)

arm.description: 'robot0' or 'robot1' on the two-arm tasks (required there); omit on one arm

Move the arm along joint-space waypoints (move_to_joints each).
